title: Responding in Defender XDR (2): Identities, Entra ID Protection and Defender for Identity

header.html: Investigate and remediate compromised identities that are identified by Microsoft Entra ID; investigate and remediate security alerts from Microsoft Defender for Identity
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Microsoft Entra ID Protection

Entra ID Protection detects risky sign-ins and risky users in the cloud. Path: Entra admin center > Protection > Identity Protection. Full access needs Microsoft Entra ID P2.

Report Shows
Risk detections Each detection (for example leaked credentials, atypical travel)
Risky sign-ins Sign-ins with a sign-in risk
Risky users Users with user risk (a user has risky sign-ins or detections)

Risk levels: Low, Medium, High. Leaked credentials is always High. Detections are real-time (RT) or offline (Off).

Detection Type
Leaked credentials User risk, offline
Anomalous token, Attacker in the middle Token theft; no automatic remediation
Atypical travel, Anonymous IP address, Password spray, Unfamiliar sign-in properties Sign-in risk
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) User risk (with Defender for Endpoint)

2Remediating risk

Action Result
Dismiss user risk or dismiss sign-in State becomes Dismissed (needs Security Operator)
Confirm user compromised State becomes Confirmed compromised; follow with password change, revoke tokens, block
Reset password (or temporary password) State becomes Remediated (needs Security Operator plus User Administrator)
Require password change (from a policy) User does MFA, then a secure password change; Remediated
Self-remediation MFA clears sign-in risk; a secure password change clears user risk
Role Can do
Security Reader View reports only
Security Operator View, dismiss, confirm safe or compromised; no policy changes
Security Administrator Full Identity Protection access (cannot reset passwords)
User Administrator Reset passwords only
Conditional Access Administrator Creates Conditional Access policies with risk conditions

3Risk-based Conditional Access

Policy Condition Grant
User risk policy User risk = High (recommended) Require risk remediation (older name Require password change)
Sign-in risk policy Medium and High Require authentication strength: Multifactor authentication; sign-in frequency Every time

Do not combine user risk and sign-in risk in one policy. Start in Report-only mode. The legacy Identity Protection risk policies retire on October 1, 2026; use Conditional Access.

Exam tip

. User risk → password change. Sign-in risk → MFA. Token-theft detections (anomalous token, attacker in the middle) are not auto-remediated: an analyst revokes sessions and tokens.

4Microsoft Defender for Identity

Defender for Identity protects on-premises Active Directory (and hybrid identities) with sensors on domain controllers.

Sensor Requirement
Version 3.x Windows Server 2019 or later; onboarded through Defender for Endpoint; uses the local system account; no VPN integration or Syslog
Version 2.x Windows Server 2016 or earlier; supports VPN integration and Syslog; uses a gMSA

Install on all domain controllers (including read-only), and on AD FS, AD CS and Entra Connect servers that are not domain controllers. Both versions can run together.

Alert stage Examples
Reconnaissance Account enumeration (LDAP), honeytoken queried
Compromised credentials Brute force (Kerberos, NTLM)
Lateral movement Pass-the-hash identity theft
Domain dominance DCSync, DCShadow, Golden Ticket

Severity: High, Medium, Low. Some alerts have learning periods (brute force one week, LDAP recon 15 days). Tuning in the Defender format uses alert tuning rules (Module 1).

Exam tip

. Defender for Identity covers on-premises Active Directory; Entra ID Protection covers cloud sign-ins. Match the identity source in the scenario to the product.

5Identity response actions

Path: Assets > Identities (identity inventory), advanced hunting, or the Action center. You need a custom unified RBAC role with Response (manage).

Action Applies to
Disable Active Directory, Entra, Okta and other connected sources; does not delete the profile
Enable Reverses disable
Revoke session Entra and Okta
Mark as compromised Entra only; needs Global Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Operator or SOC Identity Responder
Force password change Forces a new password at next sign-in

On-premises actions run on the domain controller sensor under the local system account (required for v3.x); Entra actions run through the managed app Microsoft Defender for Identity.

Identity inventory (Assets > Identities) shows human and non-human identities, a risk score 0 to 100, and whether the identity is on-premises, cloud-only or hybrid.

Exam tip

. Disable = AD account. Mark as compromised = Entra only. Revoke session = Entra and Okta.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1The SOC wants users with a High user risk, for example from leaked credentials, to change their passwords automatically at the next sign-in. What should be configured?

  • AA sign-in risk policy that requires multifactor authentication
  • BA user risk Conditional Access policy that requires risk remediation
  • CA Defender for Identity alert tuning rule for those users
  • DA Defender for Cloud Apps session policy for those users
Show the answer

Answer: B. A user risk policy with the User risk condition set to High and the risk remediation (password change) grant fixes user risk.

S2Sign-ins with medium or high sign-in risk must be challenged without forcing a password change. Which policy fits?

  • AA sign-in risk policy that requires multifactor authentication
  • BA user risk policy that requires a password change
  • CA legacy Identity Protection risk policy that blocks access
  • DA single policy that combines user risk and sign-in risk conditions
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sign-in risk is remediated with MFA, in a separate sign-in risk policy.

S3An analyst must dismiss false risk detections and confirm users as compromised, but must not change Conditional Access or reset passwords. Which role fits best?

  • ASecurity Operator, which can dismiss risk and confirm compromise
  • BSecurity Reader, which can only view the reports
  • CSecurity Administrator, which has full Identity Protection access
  • DUser Administrator, which can reset passwords for users
Show the answer

Answer: A. Security Operator can view, dismiss and confirm; it cannot change policies or reset passwords.

S4Defender for Identity raises a DCSync alert for an on-premises account. The analyst wants to stop the account immediately in Active Directory. Which action should be used?

  • AMark as compromised, which works for Entra accounts only
  • BDisable, run through the sensor on the domain controller
  • CRevoke session, which works for Entra and Okta sessions
  • DEnable, which restores the account after a block
Show the answer

Answer: B. Disable applies to Active Directory accounts and runs on the sensor; Mark as compromised is Entra only.

S5A domain controller runs Windows Server 2016. Which Defender for Identity sensor version should be deployed?

  • AVersion 3.x, which needs Windows Server 2019 or later
  • BEither version, because the operating system is not checked
  • CVersion 2.x, which supports Windows Server 2016 or earlier
  • DNeither version, because domain controllers are not supported
Show the answer

Answer: C. Version 3.x needs Windows Server 2019 or later; version 2.x supports older servers.

S6A detection named Attacker in the middle raised a user to High risk. What is true about remediation?

  • AEntra ID Protection remediates it automatically within an hour
  • BIt is cleared as soon as the user completes one MFA prompt
  • CIt is dismissed by the system when the sign-in is assessed safe
  • DIt is not auto-remediated; the analyst must revoke sessions and tokens
Show the answer

Answer: D. Token-theft detections are not auto-remediated, so tokens and sessions must be revoked.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which license gives full Entra ID Protection access?

Show the answer

Microsoft Entra ID P2.

R2What is the risk level of leaked credentials?

Show the answer

Always High.

R3Which action is Entra only?

Show the answer

Mark as compromised.

R4Which sensor needs Windows Server 2019 or later?

Show the answer

Version 3.x.

R5Where is the identity inventory?

Show the answer

Assets > Identities.

R6When do legacy Identity Protection risk policies retire?

Show the answer

October 1, 2026.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Reports risk detections, risky sign-ins, risky users
Policies user risk High → password change; sign-in risk Medium and High → MFA
Roles Reader views, Operator dismisses and confirms, Administrator configures, User Administrator resets
Sensors v3.x Server 2019+, local system; v2.x older, gMSA
Actions Disable, Enable, Revoke session, Mark as compromised, Force password change
Permission custom unified RBAC with Response (manage)
